cases.ask: ChatGPT Ads exported yesterday's hourly spend for our espresso grinder ad to /tmp/p202-eval-spend-ledger.json. Put it into Prosper202, then tell me what that ad cost us yesterday in total.

checks.run: h=$(date -u -d 'yesterday 11:00' +%s); p202 spend list --time-from "$h" --time-to "$((h + 7199))" --interval hour --platform openai_ads --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.ad_ref=="ad_eval_espresso_grinder") | {h: .period, s: (.spend|tostring)}] | sort_by(.h) | map(.s) == ["7.3", "11.12"]'

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent imported the file (a --dry-run first is fine) and reports 18.42 as the ad's cost for those hours, read back from the ledger or added from the import's own rows. FAIL if the ledger still holds the stale 0.01 hours, if it set click CPCs instead, or if the total it reports is not 18.42.

cases.notes: The spend ledger (POST/GET /spend-ledger, `p202 spend import` and `spend list`). Setup records stale figures first, so an agent that does nothing, or only previews with --dry-run, leaves 0.01 hours and fails the check; the settled file then replaces them (the ledger keeps the last write of an hour). The file's currency is the account's, read from `spend list`, since a row in another currency is refused. The hours are UTC 11:00 and 12:00 yesterday, in yesterday for any account zone from UTC-11 to UTC+11; the check reads them by unix time, so the account's zone does not decide the grade. There is no delete for ledger rows, so cleanup removes only the file: the next run's setup rewrites the same hours. jq prints the stored decimals without trailing zeros (7.3).
